consequence.statement: Existing UpdateRequest objects stay stored as v1beta1 until rewritten; the operator must run a storage version migration (re-write all objects) and update status.storedVersions before a later release removes v1beta1.
consequence.remediation: After upgrading, run a storage version migration for updaterequests.kyverno.io (re-write all UpdateRequest objects at the new storage version) and update the CRD's status.storedVersions before upgrading to a release that removes v1beta1.

original.statement: The storage version of the updaterequests.kyverno.io CRD changed from v1beta1 to v2 (v1beta1.storage true→false, v2.storage false→true between 1.12.6 and 1.13.0), so existing UpdateRequest objects stay stored as v1beta1 until rewritten and a storage version migration plus a status.storedVersions update is required before a later release removes v1beta1.

consequence.statement: Nothing fails on upgrade. The API server now stores UpdateRequest objects as v2 (v2.storage false→true, v1beta1.storage true→false). Existing objects stay stored as v1beta1 until they are rewritten, and status.storedVersions still lists v1beta1.
consequence.remediation: Optionally run a storage version migration for updaterequests.kyverno.io (rewrite all objects) and remove v1beta1 from status.storedVersions, before any future release that stops serving v1beta1.

corrected.statement: From 1.12.6 to 1.13.0 the storage version of updaterequests.kyverno.io moves from v1beta1 to v2. v1beta1 is still defined, so existing UpdateRequest objects keep working and stay stored as v1beta1 until rewritten. Objects written from now on are stored as v2.

decision.reason: The rendered diffs show only a storage flag swap for updaterequests.kyverno.io between 1.12.6 and 1.13.0: v1beta1 storage changes from true to false [ev-cf5b10ff8047] and v2 storage changes from false to true [ev-d3850c78b94e]. Nothing shows v1beta1 stops being served, gets rejected or breaks in this release. The migration step only matters "before a later release removes v1beta1", and no evidence says such a removal is scheduled. So doing nothing still works, new writes are just stored as v2, and the mandatory migration-required kind over-claims; behavior-change (review) is the supported kind.
